drills.title: The Collection Point Network
drills.prompt: A year ago Kestravel's CEO publicly told investors the company would build its own network of collection points — 200 sites in two years. Sixty are open. The economics are worse than plan. The board asks: **continue or wind down?**

exhibit.title: Kestravel: the collection point network
rows: Return on the alternative project, per annum

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"We announced it publicly — backing out damages our reputation"** | the strongest argument in the room, and it is **not monetary** | The public commitment is **already given and cannot be withdrawn** under either decision: the reputational damage from "announced and did not deliver" was incurred the moment the plan became unachievable, not at the moment of admitting it. The branch calls for an assessment of investor reaction — which is **identical under both options** as regards what has already been said, and therefore does not distinguish them |
| **"We've put in $34M"** | the monetary sunk cost, the familiar trap | The $34M is spent and does not return; a classic sunk cost, discarded by the standard rule |

**The difference between the two decoys is the slot itself.** The second is discarded mechanically by anyone who knows the rule. The first **feels different**, because it is not expressed in money.
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Future economics of the network** | "what it delivers from here" · "flow from the sites we have" · "forward cash flow" | Without future flows the decision is unsupported |
| **2. Cost of completing and cost of exiting** | "how much to reach 200" · "price of winding down" · "cost of each decision" | Without the price of both paths there is no comparison |
| **3. Alternative use of the capital** | "what instead" · "where else to invest" · "opportunity cost" | Without an alternative, "continue" is compared only against "do nothing" |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | **independent** — flow from what operates vs the cost of changing course |
| 1 ↔ 3 | **independent** |
| 2 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ partial — capital released on exit is the input to the alternative. Separated: branch 2 is the **outflow** on exit; branch 3 is the **use** of what is released |
| **Reputation ↔ 1** | ⚠️ **substitution risk** — "investors will be disappointed → revenue will fall" converts the non-monetary into the monetary **without data**. Permissible only with an estimate; a bare mention inside the flow branch is a violation |
| Reputation ↔ 2, 3 | **independent** |
| $34M ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **direct violation** — past cost inside a branch of future costs |
| $34M ↔ 1, 3 | **independent** |
| Reputation ↔ $34M | ⚠️ both are sunk, of different natures |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Future economics | flow per operating site per year · share of sites that have reached payback |
| 2. Cost of decisions | capex for the remaining sites · cost of closing the 60 · lease obligations |
| 3. Alternative | return on the nearest project using the same capital |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| size of effect | branch 2 | the remaining sites are the largest sum in the problem |
| speed of verification | branch 1 | data on the 60 operating sites exists |
| reversibility | branch 3 | capital sunk into the network does not transfer |

reference.en:
The monetary sunk cost ($34.0M) is discarded — the rule is known and the figure is explicit. **The reputational stake is not discarded**, because it does not look like a cost: it looks like an **obligation**, and obligations are meant to be honoured.

Yet it is sunk in exactly the same way: the word has been said, and the damage from a gap between word and deed arises from **the plan being unachievable**, not from admitting it. It does not distinguish between decisions about the future.

**Top echelon: NO** — a candidate who applies the rule to a non-monetary sunk item reaches the right answer. An honest **Medium**.

- notice that 19 of 60 sites have not reached payback — **31.7%** of those already open
- compute: $71.0M at the 14% alternative gives **$9.94M/year** of forgone return
- propose a third path: stop at 60 sites, neither closing nor expanding
reference.ru:
Денежный sunk cost ($34.0M) отбрасывается — правило известно, а цифра явная. **Репутационная ставка не отбрасывается**, потому что не выглядит как затрата: она выглядит как **обязательство**, а обязательства положено выполнять.

Между тем она невозвратна ровно так же: слово сказано, а ущерб от разрыва между словом и делом возникает из-за **неисполнимости плана**, а не из-за признания этого. Решения о будущем она не различает.

**Верхний эшелон: НЕТ** — кандидат, который прикладывает правило к неденежной невозвратной позиции, приходит к верному ответу. Честный **Medium**.

- заметить, что 19 из 60 площадок не вышли на payback — **31.7%** от уже открытых
- посчитать: $71.0M при альтернативе в 14% дают **$9.94M/год** упущенной доходности
- предложить третий путь: остановиться на 60 площадках, не закрывая и не расширяя

drills.title: Choosing The Distribution Centre
drills.prompt: Orvenmark is choosing a site for a distribution centre from three options. The logistics director: "We measure on average delivery cost per order — that is our headline metric. Run the numbers and name the winner."

exhibit.title: Orvenmark: three sites
exhibit.note: Delivery cost per order is calculated to the cent on the same order base for all three sites.

key.decoy:
| Suspicion | Why it's plausible | What refutes it |
|---|---|---|
| **"The calculation is wrong — they cannot be identical"** | three different sites, one identical figure looks suspicious | The calculation is correct: delivery cost is driven by the average haul, and all three sites sit at an **equal distance** from the centre of demand mass. The coincidence is substantive, not an error |
| **"Rounding hides a difference"** | the classic precision trap | The values coincide to the **second decimal**: $4.82 across all three. The note states the precision of the calculation |
| **"Not all orders were included"** | the base of comparison | The full annual volume is included: 1.42 million orders for each site |

**The key difference:** the data is clean, the question is legitimate, the metric is **appropriate** and correctly computed — it simply **does not distinguish between the options**.
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Correctness of the metric's calculation** | "is it computed right" · "check the arithmetic" · "does it reconcile" | The director explicitly asks for a check; without it the answer is incomplete |
| **2. The metric's discriminating power** | "does it distinguish the options" · "can a choice be made on it" · "is there any spread" | **Load-bearing, and this is the muscle of the slot.** A metric identical across every option **cannot** serve as a selection criterion, however correct it is |
| **3. Metrics on which the options do differ** | "what else differs" · "what to choose on" · "other criteria" | Without them the answer reduces to "no choice can be made," when a choice must be made |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | **independent** — is it computed right vs is the result useful |
| 1 ↔ 3 | **independent** |
| 2 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ partial — both concern the fitness of metrics. Separated: branch 2 concerns **this** metric; branch 3 concerns **the others** |
| Suspicions ↔ 1 | tested inside branch 1; not branches in their own right |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Correctness | delivery cost per order for each site · calculation base · precision |
| 2. Discriminating power | **spread of values across the options** · is it sufficient for a choice |
| 3. Other metrics | capex · rent · 24-hour coverage · their spread |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| the client's explicit request | branch 1 | the director asked for the calculation to be checked |
| **fitness for choosing** | branch 2 | a correct metric with no spread does not solve the task |
| size of effect | branch 3 | capex differs by a factor of 1.8 |

reference.en:
A triple inversion, the fourth state in the type where the data itself is sound.

- The data is clean — all three sites, the full volume, precision to the cent.
- The question is legitimate — a site really does need choosing.
- The metric is **appropriate** — delivery cost is relevant for a distribution centre.
- The calculation is correct — $4.82 is confirmed.

And the metric **does not distinguish the options**: the spread is zero. "The winner is X" cannot be said, not because the data is poor, but because **the chosen criterion is identical for all**.

**Top echelon: NO** — by construction, there is no defect in the data itself.

- notice that a zero spread is a **substantive result**, not a data defect
- compute: capex differs by **$6.6M**, rent by **$2.8M/year** — that is where the choice lies
- propose a criterion of total cost over 5 years: Southern $14.7 + 5×$1.8 = **$23.7M**, Northern **$25.9M**, Eastern **$31.1M** — **Southern is $7.4M cheaper than Eastern**, though on capex it looks the worst
reference.ru:
Тройная инверсия, четвёртое в типе состояние, где с самими данными всё в порядке.

- Данные чисты — все три площадки, полный объём, точность до цента.
- Вопрос законен — площадку действительно надо выбрать.
- Метрика **уместна** — для распределительного центра стоимость доставки значима.
- Расчёт верен — $4.82 подтверждается.

А метрика **не различает варианты**: разброс нулевой. Сказать «победитель — X» нельзя не потому, что данные плохи, а потому, что **выбранный критерий одинаков для всех**.

**Верхний эшелон: НЕТ** — по построению дефекта в самих данных нет.

- заметить, что нулевой разброс — это **содержательный результат**, а не дефект данных
- посчитать: разница по capex — **$6.6M**, по аренде — **$2.8M/год**; вот где лежит выбор
- предложить критерий полной стоимости за 5 лет: Southern $14.7 + 5×$1.8 = **$23.7M**, Northern **$25.9M**, Eastern **$31.1M** — **Southern дешевле Eastern на $7.4M**, хотя по capex выглядит хуже всех

drills.title: One At A Time
drills.prompt: Duskavine has three initiatives and limited management capacity — only one can run at a time. The board asks: **which do we start with?**

exhibit.title: Duskavine: three initiatives
header: What happens if the deadline is missed
rows: rollout slips, the benefit arrives later
the campaign moves to the next season
production halts until a new licence is issued

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"Start with the largest effect"** | the right criterion, correctly applied to the right quantity | The criterion is right, the quantity is right (effect in $M), the ranking is correct: ERP $2.1M → rebranding $1.8M → licence $0.4M. And the priority is **still wrong**: the first two are **reversible**, the third is not, and missing it costs not $0.4M but a production shutdown |
| **"Start with the cheapest"** | resource logic | The cost of the initiatives does not differ materially; the criterion eliminates nothing |
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Effect of each initiative** | "what it brings" · "size of the gain" · "economics" | Without the effect the prioritisation is unsupported |
| **2. Deadline and how hard it is** | "when is it needed" · "is there a hard date" · "what happens if it slips" | Without the deadline the order can be assigned arbitrarily |
| **3. Cost of error: is the decision reversible** | "what if we don't do it" · "reversibility" · "price of missing it" · "can we come back" | **Load-bearing.** Priority is set not by the size of the gain but by the **price of missing it**. A reversible initiative can be postponed and resumed; an irreversible one cannot, and its price of omission is not equal to its effect |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | **independent** — magnitude vs timing |
| 1 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **conflation risk** — "cost of error" looks like part of the effect. Separated: branch 1 is the **gain from doing it**; branch 3 is the **loss from missing it**. They are **not symmetric**: the licence delivers $0.4M and costs production |
| 2 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ partial — a hard deadline often implies irreversibility. Separated: branch 2 is **when**; branch 3 is **what happens if later** |
| Largest effect ↔ 1 | ⚠️ **duplicate** — this is branch 1 |
| Largest effect ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **opposition** — ranking by effect ignores the asymmetry in the price of omission |
| Cheapest ↔ 1 | ⚠️ partial |
| Cheapest ↔ 2, 3 | **independent** |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Effect | $M of annual gain for each initiative |
| 2. Timing | months to the deadline · how hard it is (regulatory / internal) |
| 3. Cost of error | **what happens on missing it** · is it reversible · the size of the loss, which is not the effect |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **irreversibility** | the licence | missing it halts production; the only non-recoverable item |
| deadline | the licence | 3 months against 9 and 14 |
| size of effect | ERP | $2.1M is the largest gain, but reversible |

**Starting with ERP under the criterion "size of effect" is legitimate by the letter and wrong in substance:** the criterion does not account for the asymmetry in the price of omission. An ORDER defect is recorded if the candidate **has not checked** reversibility.

reference.en:
The candidate names the criterion "largest effect" — the right criterion. He applies it to the quantity "effect in $M" — **the right quantity**. The ranking is correct: 2.1 → 1.8 → 0.4.

And the priority is still wrong, because the criterion **measures the wrong thing when setting a sequence**. Under sequential execution what matters is not the gain but the **loss from postponement**, and that is asymmetric: reversible initiatives lose time, the irreversible one loses production.

**Top echelon: YES.** The criterion is right, the quantity is right, the arithmetic is right — and the answer is wrong.

- notice: the price of missing the licence is a production halt of unknown length — its order of magnitude has to be estimated before it can be set against the $0.4M effect
- notice the deadlines run inversely to the effects: 3 < 9 < 14 against 0.4 < 1.8 < 2.1
- propose the criterion "maximum price of omission" instead of "maximum effect" for sequencing tasks
reference.ru:
Кандидат называет критерий «наибольший эффект» — верный критерий. Он прикладывает его к величине «эффект в $M» — **к верной величине**. Ранжирование верно: 2.1 → 1.8 → 0.4.

И приоритет всё равно неверен, потому что критерий **меряет не то, когда речь идёт о порядке**. При последовательном исполнении важен не выигрыш, а **потеря от откладывания**, а она асимметрична: обратимые инициативы теряют время, необратимая теряет производство.

**Верхний эшелон: ДА.** Критерий верен, величина верна, арифметика верна — а ответ неверен.

- заметить: цена упущенной лицензии — остановка производства неизвестной длины; её порядок величины надо оценить, прежде чем ставить её против эффекта в $0.4M
- заметить, что сроки идут обратно эффектам: 3 < 9 < 14 против 0.4 < 1.8 < 2.1
- предложить для задач на очерёдность критерий «максимальная цена пропуска» вместо «максимального эффекта»

drills.title: Demand Above Capacity
drills.prompt: Demand for Pellworth's products exceeds capacity by **34%**. The operations director: "Tell me how we add capacity."

exhibit.title: Pellworth: options for covering the 34% shortfall

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"Pick the best of the three options by NPV"** | three options are named, all costed, the ranking is correct | The ranking is correct **within the list**, and the list is **incomplete**: the axis "way of obtaining capacity" admits a fourth option — **do not add it**. The branch calls for the NPV of three options and will not reveal that the comparison needs a fourth |
| **"Check the financing"** | the resource reflex | All three options fit within the limit; the branch eliminates nothing |
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Ways of obtaining capacity** | "options" · "alternatives" · "how we could add it" | Without a list there is no choice |
| **2. Economics of each way** | "NPV" · "return" · "what it costs" | Without economics the options are not comparable |
| **3. Completeness of the option space** | "are all the ways named" · "is the list closed" · "is there a do-nothing option" | **Load-bearing.** A list of three ways of **adding** capacity omits the option of not adding it, and that option is not in the exhibit at all — the candidate has to name it. "Build the plant" is unsupported until it has been compared against declining to grow |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | **independent** — the list vs the economics |
| 1 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **conflation risk** — both concern the list. Separated: branch 1 is **which ways exist**; branch 3 is **whether all ways are there, including refusal** |
| 2 ↔ 3 | **independent** |
| NPV of three ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **duplicate** — this is branch 2 applied to an incomplete set |
| NPV of three ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **opposition** — a ranking presupposes the list is complete |
| Financing ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **absorption** |
| Financing ↔ 1, 3 | **independent** |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Ways | the list of options · resources each requires |
| 2. Economics | NPV of each option · time to capacity |
| 3. Completeness | **the axis of enumeration** · whether the set is closed on that axis · whether a "do nothing" option is present |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **completeness of the set** | branch 3 | ranking an incomplete list gives the wrong answer however precise it is |
| size of effect | branch 2 | NPV ranks them |
| speed of verification | branch 1 | the list can be drawn without data |

reference.en:
The question is framed as "**how do we add** capacity," and that framing **narrows the space** to ways of adding. The candidate names three, all correct, all independent, all costed — and the list looks exhaustive, because it exhausts the **stated** axis.

The fourth option lies on the same real axis ("bring demand and capacity into balance") and requires no capex and has to be costed before the three named options can be ranked.

**Top echelon: YES.** Three options are named correctly, are independent, are costed correctly and ranked correctly — and the answer is wrong, because the set is incomplete.

- notice that the question "how do we add" **itself narrows** the space — reframe it as "how do we bring demand and capacity into balance"
- compute: leasing covers **19 of 34 pp**, i.e. **55.9%** of the shortfall — the only partial option
- propose a combination: price plus leasing, if the shortfall must be closed quickly and in full
reference.ru:
Вопрос поставлен как «**как нам добавить** мощность», и такая рамка **сужает пространство** до способов добавления. Кандидат называет три, все верны, все независимы, все просчитаны, — и список выглядит исчерпывающим, потому что исчерпывает **заявленную** ось.

Четвёртый вариант лежит на той же настоящей оси («привести спрос и мощность в равновесие»), не требует capex, и его надо просчитать прежде, чем три названных варианта можно ранжировать.

**Верхний эшелон: ДА.** Три варианта названы верно, независимы, просчитаны верно и ранжированы верно, — а ответ неверен, потому что набор неполон.

- заметить, что вопрос «как нам добавить» **сам сужает** пространство — переформулировать его как «как нам привести спрос и мощность в равновесие»
- посчитать: лизинг закрывает **19 из 34 п.п.**, то есть **55.9%** дефицита — единственный частичный вариант
- предложить комбинацию: цена плюс лизинг, если дефицит надо закрыть быстро и целиком

mehanizm.correct: достраивает ось способами закрыть разрыв, включая отказ от расширения, и только потом сравнивает

drills.title: The Distributor Channel
drills.prompt: Grenvalt's revenue fell 17.6% over the year. The sales director: "The distributor channel market contracted by a third — that is an external shock, it is not our doing." The board asks: **is that so?**

exhibit.title: Grenvalt: revenue by channel and the market
rows: Our share of the distribution channel

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"Confirm the external shock with industry statistics"** | the director has supplied a ready hypothesis with a figure | The statistics **will confirm** the channel contraction: −32.6%, the fact is correct. The branch calls for data that **proves the phenomenon is external** and will not show that it was caused by our own decision. Confirmation of a correct figure under a wrong attribution of cause |
| **"Compare against competitors in the same channel"** | the second reflex | Competitors in the channel grew — the branch will indicate that it is not purely external, but will not explain the mechanism |
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. External: market dynamics** | "the market" · "industry backdrop" · "category demand" | Without the market the scale of the external effect cannot be assessed |
| **2. Internal: our share and its movement** | "share" · "our result relative to the market" · "position" | Without share the external explains everything |
| **3. The cause of the "external" itself** | "what caused the contraction" · "who created it" · "our own past decisions" · "the boundary of external" | **Load-bearing, and this is the muscle of the slot.** A phenomenon assigned to the external may be a **consequence of our own decision**. Then the boundary between external and internal has been drawn wrongly, and "it is not our doing" is unsupported |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **conflation risk** — share is the ratio of ours to the market. Separated: branch 1 is the **absolute** trend; branch 2 the **relative** position |
| 1 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **the slot's key pair** — "market dynamics" and "the cause of those dynamics" look like one branch. Separated: branch 1 is **what happened** to the market; branch 3 is **why**, and whether we did it. A candidate who merges them accepts the external as given |
| 2 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ partial — share loss and our decision are linked. Separated: branch 2 is the **measurement** of position; branch 3 the **causal link** to our action |
| Statistics ↔ 1 | ⚠️ **duplicate** — this is branch 1 |
| Statistics ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **opposition** — confirming a fact is not establishing a cause |
| Competitors ↔ 2 | ⚠️ partial |
| Competitors ↔ 1, 3 | **independent** |
| Statistics ↔ Competitors | **independent** |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Market | channel volume by year · trend of the whole category |
| 2. Share | our share by channel · our rate against the market's |
| 3. Cause of the external | **dates of our decisions against dates of the contraction** · counterparty behaviour after our action |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **testing the client's hypothesis** | branch 3 | the director has already supplied an attribution; that is what is being tested |
| speed of verification | branch 1 | industry statistics are public |
| size of effect | branch 2 | share shows whether this is our result |

reference.en:
The candidate performs **the correct operation** — separating external from internal. And the separation confirms the director's hypothesis: the channel market really did contract 32.6%, an external fact.

The error is in the **boundary**: the channel contraction was caused in part by our own launch of direct sales. The phenomenon has been assigned to the external **by where it is observed**, not by its cause. We fall faster than the channel market (−46.5% against −32.6%), lose share within it (−3.0 pp), and grow in direct sales at the same time (+21.3%).

**Top echelon: YES.** The separation is performed correctly, the external fact is confirmed — and the conclusion "it is not our doing" is wrong.

- notice we fall **13.9 pp faster** than the channel market (−46.5% against −32.6%) — so there is a contribution of ours on top of the general one
- compute the net effect: direct +$29.2M against distribution −$85.6M, i.e. **−$56.4M**
- propose assessing whether the growth of the direct channel compensates the loss of distribution over the horizon — at present it does not
reference.ru:
Кандидат выполняет **верную операцию** — отделяет внешнее от внутреннего. И разделение подтверждает гипотезу директора: канальный рынок действительно сжался на 32.6% — внешний факт.

Ошибка — в **границе**: сжатие канала отчасти вызвано нашим же запуском прямых продаж. Явление отнесено к внешнему **по месту наблюдения**, а не по причине. Мы падаем быстрее канального рынка (−46.5% против −32.6%), теряем долю внутри него (−3.0 пп) и одновременно растём в прямых продажах (+21.3%).

**Верхний эшелон: ДА.** Разделение выполнено верно, внешний факт подтверждён — а вывод «это не наших рук дело» неверен.

- заметить, что мы падаем на **13.9 пп быстрее** канального рынка (−46.5% против −32.6%), — значит, поверх общего есть и наш собственный вклад
- посчитать чистый эффект: прямые +$29.2M против дистрибуции −$85.6M, то есть **−$56.4M**
- предложить оценить, компенсирует ли рост прямого канала потерю дистрибуции на горизонте, — сейчас не компенсирует

mehanizm.correct: проверяет, какая часть падения произведена собственным решением о распределении продаж по каналам

drills.title: Five Percent On Price
drills.prompt: Yarnstead's board requires profit to be maximised over three years. Management proposes raising prices by 5% — "the best option on profit." The board asks: **is it the best?**

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"Check management's calculation"** | the natural first reaction to someone else's recommendation | Management's calculation is **correct**: raising prices delivers the highest profit **in year one** ($16.8M). The branch calls for their workings and will confirm them. The divergence is not in the arithmetic but in the **objective function** |
| **"Assess the competitor response"** | the market reflex | The competitor response is already embedded in the yearly forecasts; the branch duplicates the exhibit |
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. The result of each option by year** | "profit by year" · "option trajectories" · "what each delivers" | Without a yearly breakdown the objective functions are indistinguishable |
| **2. The board's objective function** | "what the board maximises" · "a three-year horizon" · "the sum over the period" | Without stating the board's objective the comparison is arbitrary |
| **3. Management's objective function and how it differs** | "what management maximises" · "whose objective is being optimised" · "do the parties' objectives coincide" | **Load-bearing, and this is the muscle of the slot.** Both parties optimise **correctly**, but **different** functions: the board the three-year sum, management the first-year result. "Management made a mistake" is unsupported — they made none, they are solving a different problem |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | **independent** — the data vs the criterion |
| 1 ↔ 3 | **independent** |
| 2 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **the slot's key pair** — two objective functions on the same data. Separated: branch 2 is the **three-year sum**; branch 3 is the **first year**. A candidate who runs a single "company objective" will not see the divergence |
| Check the calculation ↔ 1 | ⚠️ **duplicate** — this is branch 1 |
| Check the calculation ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **opposition** — a correct calculation does not imply a correct objective |
| Competitors ↔ 1 | ⚠️ **absorption** — the response is embedded in the forecasts |
| Competitors ↔ 2, 3 | **independent** |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Result | profit of each option in each year |
| 2. Board's objective | **the three-year sum** for each option · the optimum |
| 3. Management's objective | **the first year** for each option · the optimum · what sets management's horizon |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **fit to the objective** | branch 2 | without an explicit objective function no comparison is possible |
| size of effect | branch 1 | the data supplies the magnitudes |
| speed of verification | branch 3 | management's horizon follows from the incentive scheme |

reference.en:
Management **is not making a mistake**. Its calculation is correct, the data is agreed, and option C really does deliver the highest first-year profit — **$16.8M** against $14.2M and $9.6M.

The divergence lies in the **objective function**: the board maximises the three-year sum, where the best option is **B ($50.7M)**, while management maximises the first year, where the best is **C ($16.8M)**. Both optimisations are correct, and both parties are right **within their own problem**.

**Top echelon: NO** — a candidate who asks "which quantity are we maximising" reaches the right answer. An honest **Medium**.

- notice the divergence is worth **$8.8M** over three years (50.7 against 41.9)
- compute: option B loses to C by **$7.2M** in the first year — that is the price of patience
- propose a solution that is not analytical but **organisational**: tie part of the remuneration to the three-year result
reference.ru:
Менеджмент **не ошибается**. Его расчёт верен, данные согласованы, и вариант C действительно даёт наибольшую прибыль первого года — **$16.8M** против $14.2M и $9.6M.

Расхождение лежит в **целевой функции**: совет директоров максимизирует трёхлетнюю сумму, где лучший вариант — **B ($50.7M)**, а менеджмент максимизирует первый год, где лучший — **C ($16.8M)**. Обе оптимизации верны, и обе стороны правы **внутри своей задачи**.

**Верхний эшелон: НЕТ** — кандидат, который спрашивает «какую величину мы максимизируем», приходит к верному ответу. Честный **Medium**.

- заметить, что расхождение составляет **$8.8M** за три года (50.7 против 41.9)
- посчитать: вариант B проигрывает C **$7.2M** в первый год — это цена терпения
- предложить решение не аналитическое, а **организационное**: привязать часть вознаграждения к трёхлетнему результату

mehanizm.correct: проверяет, на каком горизонте максимизируется прибыль, и сравнивает варианты на объявленном советом горизонте

drills.title: The New Formulation
drills.prompt: Wrenlocke is converting production to a new formulation. The project runs **24 months** and delivers **+$3.2M** cumulatively. The board asks: **do we launch?**

exhibit.title: Wrenlocke: conversion to the new formulation, $M

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"The result is positive — launch"** | a direct inference from the total | The total is correct: +$3.2M over 24 months. But mid-horizon there is an **irreversible step**, after which exit is impossible, and by that moment the accumulated loss is at its maximum. The branch calls for the headline figure and **will not show the trajectory** |
| **"Compare against alternative projects"** | the portfolio reflex | A comparison is appropriate but does not answer the question about the structure of risk **inside** this project |
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. The final result** | "what the project delivers" · "cumulative total" · "sum over the horizon" | Without the total the decision is unsupported |
| **2. The trajectory within the horizon** | "how it runs by month" · "the accumulation profile" · "where the minimum sits" | Without the trajectory the total conceals risk: an identical total can have very different profiles |
| **3. Points of irreversibility** | "where exit becomes impossible" · "after which step is there no way back" · "reversibility by stage" | **Load-bearing, and this is the muscle of the slot.** The project is reversible up to a certain step and irreversible after it. "Launch" is unsupported without answering **what we are risking at the point of no return** |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **conflation risk** — the total is the last point of the trajectory. Separated: branch 1 is the **value at the end**; branch 2 is the **profile in between** |
| 1 ↔ 3 | **independent** — magnitude vs reversibility |
| 2 ↔ 3 | ⚠️ **the slot's key pair** — the point of no return lies **on** the trajectory. Separated: branch 2 is **where the cumulative minimum sits**; branch 3 is **where the option to exit disappears**. Whether they coincide is the subject of the check |
| Positive total ↔ 1 | ⚠️ **duplicate** |
| Positive total ↔ 2, 3 | ⚠️ **opposition** — the total shows neither the profile nor the reversibility |
| Alternatives ↔ 1 | ⚠️ partial |
| Alternatives ↔ 2, 3 | **independent** |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Total | cumulative result at month 24 |
| 2. Trajectory | cumulative total by month · month of the minimum · month it turns positive |
| 3. Irreversibility | the month after which exit is impossible · the accumulated loss at that moment · what is lost on exiting before and after |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **irreversibility** | branch 3 | the cost of error is set by the point of no return, not by the total |
| size of effect | branch 2 | the profile shows the maximum loss |
| speed of verification | branch 1 | the total is already computed |

reference.en:
The total is correct and positive: **+$3.2M** over 24 months. The horizon is chosen correctly — 24 months, the whole project. The sequence of effects is accounted for: costs first, returns after.

The error is that **mid-horizon there is a point of no return**, and it falls exactly on the **maximum accumulated loss**: at month 8 the figure is **−$11.2M**, and from month 9 exit also means reinstating a line that has been dismantled — a cost the client has to be asked for.

The project therefore asks for agreement not to "+$3.2M over two years" but to "−$11.2M with the right to change our minds forfeited, in exchange for +$3.2M in 24 months."

**Top echelon: NO** — a candidate who checks reversibility stage by stage reaches the right answer. An honest **Medium**.

- notice that the month of the minimum and the month reversibility is lost **coincide** — the worst possible combination
- compute: exiting at month 9 costs 11.2 + 19.4 = **$30.6M** against $11.2M at month 8
- propose moving the dismantling of the old line to month 12 if technically possible: the point of no return would then fall beyond the minimum
reference.ru:
Итог верен и положителен: **+$3.2M** за 24 месяца. Горизонт выбран верно — 24 месяца, весь проект. Последовательность эффектов учтена: сначала затраты, отдача потом.

Ошибка в том, что **в середине горизонта есть точка невозврата**, и она приходится ровно на **максимум накопленного убытка**: на 8-м месяце цифра — **−$11.2M**, а с 9-го месяца выход означает ещё и восстановление демонтированной линии — затрату, которую надо запросить у клиента.

Значит, проект просит согласия не на «+$3.2M за два года», а на «−$11.2M с утратой права передумать в обмен на +$3.2M через 24 месяца».

**Верхний эшелон: НЕТ** — кандидат, который проверяет обратимость этап за этапом, приходит к верному ответу. Честный **Medium**.

- заметить, что месяц минимума и месяц утраты обратимости **совпадают** — худшее из возможных сочетаний
- посчитать: выход на 9-м месяце стоит 11.2 + 19.4 = **$30.6M** против $11.2M на 8-м
- предложить перенести демонтаж старой линии на 12-й месяц, если это технически возможно: тогда точка невозврата ляжет за минимумом

mehanizm.correct: принимает решение по траектории накопленного результата и по точке, после которой выход невозможен
mehanizm.why: положительный итог за горизонт не говорит, что происходит в середине пути

drills.title: The Same Fifty Percent
drills.family_note: круг 40: 50% и 40% — доли ПЛАТЕЖЕЙ, а не доли людей; решение принимается о людях, и состав группы в записи не установлен
drills.prompt:
Verendal has 60 million subscribers. Collections cost the company money, and a team has proposed removing the two worst credit bands from the customer book. The team's summary is in the Exhibit.

**Where would you start the analysis, and why?**

exhibit.title: Team summary: the two lowest credit bands
rows: Band 500–549: share of bills paid late
Next band up: share of customer base
Next band up: share of bills paid late

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"Recompute the saving"** — margin on $75 × 6.0M against $50 × 45% × 6.0M | the table hands over every input, and the arithmetic is the visible task | The branch is **relevant and premature**. It prices a decision whose object is not established: the 50% and 40% are shares **of bills**, not shares **of people**. Until the book says whether the same customers are late every month or different ones each month, the multiplication is over a group that may not exist. That is the muscle of the slot |
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Composition of the late payments** | "is it the same people" · "repeat vs occasional" · "who inside the band" | Decides whether removal targets customers or events. Without it the saving is computed over an assumed cohort |
| **2. Economics of the retained customer** | "margin per subscriber" · "cost to serve" · "revenue lost on exit" | The $75 bill and the 25% margin are lost with the customer, the $50 of collections is only spent on a customer who goes late — two different frequencies on the same person |
| **3. Levers short of removal** | "late fee" · "collection cadence" · "deposit or prepay" · "credit screen at signup" | The company charges no late fee and collects monthly; the proposal jumps to the most irreversible option before the cheap ones are priced |
| **4. What 6.0M customers are worth beyond their bills** | "scale" · "network position" · "share against the number two" | Removal moves the base from 60M to 54M; the value of scale is not in the table and is not zero |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | **independent** — one is who they are, the other is what they earn |
| 1 ↔ 3 | **independent** — composition does not depend on the lever chosen |
| 2 ↔ 4 | ⚠️ partial — both are value of the customer. Separated: branch 2 is value **on the bill**, branch 4 is value **off the bill** |
key.order: Branch 1. The decision removes **people**; the evidence describes **payments**. Everything downstream — the saving, the choice of lever, the scale argument — is priced differently depending on whether the late bills sit on a stable minority or is spread thinly across the whole 6.0M. Any other branch is a defensible start as well when the candidate names a real criterion for it — size of effect, speed to check, or cost of data; Branch 1 is the start the record forces, not the only one permitted.
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Composition | **distinct customers behind the late bills, not the 50% and 40% shares of bills** · late bills per customer per year · share of the 6.0M late every month against late once |
| 2. Customer economics | the $75 bill at a 25% margin, lost per customer removed · the $50 of collections, spent only per customer chased · how often in a year that $50 falls on the same person |
| 3. Cheaper levers | a late fee, none charged today · cost of the monthly collection cadence · share of the 6.0M a deposit or a signup credit screen would cover |
| 4. Value beyond the bill | base before and after removal, 60M → 54M · our share against the number two · what a subscriber is worth outside the $75 bill |

reference.en:
**Start with the composition of the late payments, because the proposal removes customers while the evidence counts bills.**

The table gives 50% and 40% as shares of **bills paid late**, and the team converts them into a block of **6.0M people** to be removed. Those are two different objects. If a stable minority inside each band is late every month, removal is aimed at them and the saving is real and concentrated. If lateness rotates across the band, removal deletes mostly customers who pay — the company loses **$75** bills at a **25%** margin from people who cost it nothing, and keeps the collections problem in whatever cohort remains.

The book puts the question and refuses to settle it: *"Is it the same 50 percent who pay late every month? — Not necessarily. You can assume that everyone in that group has been late paying the bill at some point, some more than others."* That sentence is the case: the group is defined by an event, not by a type.

Only after that does the arithmetic mean anything, and only then do the cheaper levers get priced — there is **no late fee** at all today, and collections run every month at a **$50** cost per customer chased.

**Source:** `Case-in-Point-2013`, the wireless late-payment case: 1% of the base in the 500–549 band late on 50% of bills · 9% of the base in the next band late on 40% · 6 million customers proposed for removal out of 60 million · average bill $40 overall and $75 in these bands · $50 to collect from one late-paying customer · 25% profit margin · no late fee charged.
reference.ru:
**Начни с состава просрочек, потому что предложение убирает клиентов, тогда как свидетельство считает счета.**

Таблица даёт 50% и 40% как доли **счетов, оплаченных с опозданием**, а команда превращает их в блок из **6.0M человек**, которых надо убрать. Это два разных объекта. Если внутри каждой полосы опаздывает каждый месяц устойчивое меньшинство, удаление нацелено именно на него и экономия реальна и сконцентрирована. Если же опоздание гуляет по полосе, удаление стирает в основном тех, кто платит, — компания теряет счета по **$75** с маржой **25%** от людей, которые ей ничего не стоят, и оставляет проблему взыскания в той когорте, что останется.

Книга ставит вопрос и отказывается его решать: *«Те ли это самые 50 процентов, которые платят с опозданием каждый месяц? — Не обязательно. Можешь считать, что каждый в этой группе хотя бы раз опаздывал с оплатой счёта, кто-то чаще, кто-то реже.»* Эта фраза и есть кейс: группа задана событием, а не типом.

Только после этого арифметика что-то значит, и только тогда более дешёвые рычаги получают цену — сегодня **штрафа за просрочку** нет вовсе, а взыскание идёт каждый месяц и стоит **$50** на одного клиента, с которого взыскивают.

**Источник:** `Case-in-Point-2013`, кейс о просрочке платежей у оператора беспроводной связи: 1% базы в полосе 500–549 опаздывает по 50% счетов · 9% базы в следующей полосе опаздывает по 40% · 6 миллионов клиентов предложено убрать из 60 миллионов · средний счёт $40 в целом и $75 в этих полосах · $50 на взыскание с одного опаздывающего клиента · маржа прибыли 25% · штраф за просрочку не взимается.

mehanizm.correct: устанавливает, к чему относится доля просрочек — к счетам или к людям — прежде чем умножать
mehanizm.why: доля от счетов не переносится на число людей без данных о повторяемости

drills.title: The Salary On The Note
drills.family_note: Корпус F3. В записи прямо сказано: «The **$150,000** is a measured property of the people the **$50,000** price let in» — то есть наблюдаемая величина описывает состав группы, а не действие модели. И второе: «the new price is what forms the new group — applicants move from **2,000** to **3,600**» — воздействие меняет отбор, поэтому старая база несопоставима. Входное движение отличается от ST-049 (там доли платежей против долей людей в уже существующей базе) и от BR-049 (там добровольный вход хвоста базы в опциональный продукт при неизменной базе): здесь база заменяется целиком, а число старой базы переносится в новую модель как её собственный результат.
drills.prompt:
Marrowbridge College is a liberal arts college serving about **4,000 students**. Facing declining enrolment, the President wants to abolish tuition outright and replace it with a binding commitment: every graduate pays **5%** of annual income back to the college for the entirety of their career.

The admissions office has surveyed the districts the college recruits from and produced the forecast in the Exhibit. The finance office has already priced both models, per student and per entering class.

**Where would you start the analysis, and why?**
drills.anchor_metric: lifetime value per class, proposed model = $180M

exhibit.title: Marrowbridge College: current model against the proposed model, as priced by finance
rows: Financial aid, share of total tuition
Graduate's commitment, share of annual income
Discount rate used for the commitment
Lifetime value per student, as priced
Lifetime value per entering class, as priced
exhibit.note: Average alumni salary for Marrowbridge College is currently $150,000 per year.

key.decoy:
| Branch | Why it's reflexive | [DEC-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **"$180M against $132M — adopt the proposed model"** | the two priced figures are laid side by side and invite subtraction | Both figures are arithmetically clean. But they are not built on the same people: **$132,000** is what a **current** student pays, and **$150,000** is what a **current** alumnus earns. The branch asks for the comparison and **will not ask who was measured** |
| **"Model the cash-flow gap during the transition"** | the finance reflex — tuition stops today, income arrives over careers | A real constraint and a legitimate second question. It concerns **when** the money lands, not **whose income** was used to size it |
| **"Test the perpetuity — the 5% giving rate and the 5% discount rate cancel"** | the technical reflex, and the cancellation is elegant enough to feel like the catch | The cancellation is correct: at equal rates the per-student value equals the salary exactly. That is precisely why an error **in the salary** passes into the answer at full size and unchallenged |
key.cover:
| Branch | Synonyms (≥3) | [COV-JUST] |
|---|---|---|
| **1. What each model charges a student** | "the per-student mechanics" · "how a student converts into money" · "price against claim on income" | Without it there is no comparison at all: **$50,000** less **34%** aid over **4** years against **5%** of a career |
| **2. Who the entering class is made of** | "where the extra applicants come from" · "the mix of fields of study" · "whose salary the $150,000 is" · "what the old price kept out" | **Load-bearing, and this is the muscle of the slot.** The **$150,000** is a measured property of the people the **$50,000** price let in. The new price is what forms the new group — applicants move from **2,000** to **3,600** — so the salary has to be re-measured on the body the new price brings in, not carried across |
| **3. Whether the promised money arrives** | "collection over a career" · "enforceability of the commitment" · "attrition of the claim" · "what regulators allow" | A claim held for the entirety of a career is an asset only if it is collectable; without it branch 1 prices a promise rather than a payment |
key.me:
| Pair | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **the slot's key pair** — both look like "the value of a student". Separated: branch 1 is **the rule applied to a student**; branch 2 is **which student the rule is applied to**. The record supplies the rule cleanly and leaves the population unstated |
| 1 ↔ 3 | **independent** — the size of the claim against its collectability |
| 2 ↔ 3 | **independent** — who is in the class against whether they pay |
| "$180M vs $132M" ↔ 1 | ⚠️ **duplicate** — it is branch 1 already executed |
| "$180M vs $132M" ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **opposition** — the comparison is only valid once branch 2 is answered, and stating it first closes the question |
| Cash-flow gap ↔ 3 | ⚠️ partial — timing is one part of collection, not the whole of it |
| Cash-flow gap ↔ 2 | **independent** |
| Perpetuity check ↔ 1 | ⚠️ **duplicate** |
| Perpetuity check ↔ 2 | ⚠️ **opposition** — verifying the formula certifies the arithmetic and leaves the input untouched |
key.drive:
| Branch | What to measure |
|---|---|
| 1. Per-student mechanics | tuition collected after aid · years of study · committed share of income · discount rate |
| 2. Composition of the class | fields of study as a share of the **future** student body · average salary within each field · the weighted average that results · the same split for today's alumni, for comparison |
| 3. Collection | share of graduates actually paying · years the claim survives · regulatory and accreditation limits on a lifetime claim |
key.order:
| Criterion | Legitimate start | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **the figure the decision rests on** | branch 2 | the whole gap between **$180M** and **$132M** sits inside one input, and that input was measured on a different group |
| size of effect | branch 1 | the per-student rule scales by 1,200 students |
| speed of verification | branch 3 | collection can be checked against comparable programmes without new survey work |

reference.en:
**Conclusion.** Start by establishing who the **$150,000** was measured on — it belongs to alumni admitted under the **$50,000** price, and the proposed model's whole advantage rests on carrying it across to a class the proposed model itself creates.

**Facts.** The per-student mechanics are sound on both sides: **$50,000** less **34%** aid is **$33,000** a year, **4** years, **$132,000**; and because the **5%** commitment equals the **5%** discount rate, the proposed model's per-student value equals the graduate's salary exactly. That equality is the exposure: any error in the salary passes through undamped. The salary on the page is today's, and the policy that produces the **$180M** is the same policy that moves applicants from **2,000** to **3,600**. The gap the proposal is sold on — **$180M** against the current **$132M** — is **$48M** a class, **36.4%** above today's.

**Re-measured on the body the new price attracts** — **50%** social science at **$100k**, **25%** STEM at **$175k**, **25%** humanities at **$75k** — the average is **$112,500**, so the per-student value is **$112,500** and the class is worth **1,200** × **$112,500** = **$135M** against the current **$132M**: a **2%** difference. The decision is a toss-up on money, and has to be made on mission and on cash.

**Risk.** Internal: the college has no measurement of the new body's earnings other than a district survey, so the **$112,500** is a forecast and not an observation. External: a lifetime claim on graduate income invites scrutiny from accreditors and the Department of Education, and the claim is only worth what can be collected across a career.

**Next step.** Ask admissions for the projected field-of-study mix and the salary attached to each field before any comparison is presented to the board — and ask finance to re-run the class comparison on that mix rather than on current alumni.

**Source:** Darden Case Book 2024-25, Hooville College, pp. 53–60 — Exhibit 1 (2,000/3,600 applicants, 50%/33% acceptance, $50,000/$0 tuition, 34% financial aid, note "Average alumni salary for Hooville College is currently $150,000 per year"), Question 1 ($33,000 × 4 = $132,000; $150,000 × 0.05 / 0.05 = $150,000; $132M and $180M per class), Exhibit 2 and Question 2 (50% social science $100k, 25% STEM $175k, 25% humanities $75k → $112.5k; 1,200 × $112,500 = $135M, a 2% increase).
reference.ru:
**Вывод.** Начни с того, чтобы установить, на ком измерены **$150,000**: они относятся к выпускникам, принятым по цене **$50,000**, а всё преимущество предложенной модели держится на переносе этой цифры на курс, который предложенная модель сама и создаёт.

**Факты.** Механика в расчёте на студента верна с обеих сторон: **$50,000** минус **34%** помощи — это **$33,000** в год, **4** года, **$132,000**; а поскольку обязательство в **5%** равно ставке дисконтирования **5%**, стоимость одного студента в предложенной модели в точности равна зарплате выпускника. Это равенство и есть уязвимость: любая ошибка в зарплате проходит насквозь без затухания. Зарплата на странице — сегодняшняя, а политика, которая даёт **$180M**, — та же самая политика, которая двигает абитуриентов с **2,000** до **3,600**. Разрыв, на котором продают предложение, — **$180M** против нынешних **$132M** — это **$48M** на курс, на **36.4%** выше сегодняшнего.

**Если пересчитать на том составе, который привлекает новая цена** — **50%** социальных наук по **$100k**, **25%** STEM по **$175k**, **25%** гуманитариев по **$75k**, — среднее равно **$112,500**, поэтому стоимость одного студента — **$112,500**, а курс стоит **1,200** × **$112,500** = **$135M** против нынешних **$132M**: разница в **2%**. В деньгах решение — ничья, и принимать его придётся по миссии и по денежному потоку.

**Риск.** Внутренний: у колледжа нет измерения заработков нового состава, кроме окружного опроса, поэтому **$112,500** — это прогноз, а не наблюдение. Внешний: пожизненное требование к доходу выпускника притягивает внимание аккредитаторов и Министерства образования, а само требование стоит ровно столько, сколько удастся собрать за карьеру.

**Следующий шаг.** Запросить у приёмной комиссии прогнозный микс по направлениям обучения и зарплату по каждому направлению, прежде чем любое сравнение будет вынесено на совет, — и попросить финансовую службу пересчитать сравнение курсов на этом миксе, а не на нынешних выпускниках.

**Источник:** Darden Case Book 2024-25, Hooville College, стр. 53–60 — Exhibit 1 (2,000/3,600 абитуриентов, 50%/33% зачисления, плата $50,000/$0, 34% финансовой помощи, пометка «Средняя зарплата выпускника Hooville College сейчас составляет $150,000 в год»), Вопрос 1 ($33,000 × 4 = $132,000; $150,000 × 0.05 / 0.05 = $150,000; $132M и $180M на курс), Exhibit 2 и Вопрос 2 (50% социальных наук $100k, 25% STEM $175k, 25% гуманитариев $75k → $112.5k; 1,200 × $112,500 = $135M, рост на 2%).
